sections.title: The Sealing of the 144,000
observations: In this section, we see the significance of the sealing of the 144,000 servants of God from the tribes of Israel. This sealing represents God's protection and ownership over His people during the tumultuous times described in Revelation.
The number 144,000 is symbolic, representing completeness and the fullness of God's people. It emphasizes that God knows and preserves His own, even in the midst of judgment.

sections.title: The Great Multitude in White Robes
observations: Following the sealing, John sees a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, tribe, people, and language. This vision highlights the inclusivity of God's salvation plan, extending beyond Israel to all nations.

The imagery of white robes signifies purity and righteousness, which are granted to believers through Christ's sacrifice. This multitude stands before the throne of God, worshiping Him, which underscores the central theme of worship in Revelation.

importantVerses.commentary: This verse emphasizes the diversity of God's people, showing that salvation is available to all, regardless of background or ethnicity.
This verse assures believers of God's presence and care, promising that He will wipe away every tear, symbolizing comfort and hope in the midst of suffering.

questions: What does the sealing of the 144,000 signify for the church today?
How does the vision of the great multitude challenge our understanding of God's plan for salvation?
In what ways can we find comfort in the promise that God will wipe away every tear?
